cards.front: What do assistance features like auto braking and blind-spot watch require of you?
cards.back: Assistance features like auto braking, blind-spot watch, and crash warnings raise safety only when used right within their limits, and you must still drive unassisted since tech can fail, need shutoff, or vanish in another car.

cards.front: Which helpers may run during the driving test?
cards.back: Test day welcomes safety helpers such as backup cameras but bars convenience helpers such as adaptive cruise.

cards.front: Which warning systems are permitted on test day?
cards.back: Permitted warning systems span backup alerts, blind-spot monitors, rear, sideview, and surround cameras, curve-speed warnings, bike, pedestrian, and obstacle detection, crash warnings, speed alerts, lane-departure warnings, parking sensors, and rear cross-traffic alerts.

cards.front: Which acting assists are permitted on test day, and which stay banned?
cards.back: Permitted assists cover auto emergency braking, auto reverse braking, lane keeping, and left-turn crash avoidance, while adaptive cruise and auto parallel parking stay banned.

cards.front: How does test day treat safety helpers versus convenience helpers?
cards.back: Test day welcomes safety helpers like backup cameras, while convenience helpers like adaptive cruise stay barred.

cards.front: How many warning systems versus acting assists earn test-day approval?
cards.back: A long warning roster earns test-day approval, while only four acting assists join them.

cards.front: Why may no convenience feature run during the driving test?
cards.back: Convenience features demand no testable skill, so none may run during the driving test.

cards.front: How should you learn a car's new features?
cards.back: Study the owner manual for every new feature and quiz the dealer on leftovers.

cards.front: How do convenience features and the owner manual relate to test day and learning?
cards.back: Conveniences sit out test day entirely, while the owner manual stays required reading.

cards.front: What do warning systems do and not do?
cards.back: Warning systems flash, beep, or buzz about looming crashes or faults yet stay mostly passive, leaving the save to you.

cards.front: Who prevents the crash when a warning system sounds?
cards.back: Warning systems stay passive announcers, while the driver stays the actor who prevents the crash.

cards.front: What do backup warnings do, and what do you still do?
cards.back: Backup warnings scan astern in reverse with sound or buzz, yet you still work side mirrors, rearview, head turns, and cameras.

cards.front: What do blind-spot monitors do, and what does a lane change still demand?
cards.back: Blind-spot monitors flag hidden alongside cars by symbol, sound, or buzz with extra scolding if you signal into them, yet lane changes still demand mirrors, head turns, and the monitor together.

cards.front: Where do backup warnings and blind-spot warnings each scan?
cards.back: Backup warnings scan astern in reverse, while blind-spot warnings scan alongside for lane changes.

cards.front: What do rear cameras show, and what do they never replace?
cards.back: Rear cameras paint a wide astern view on consoles, mirrors, or visors in reverse, yet never replace mirrors and head turns.

cards.front: What do sideview cameras stream, and when may they sleep?
cards.back: Sideview cameras stream the beside lane on signal or button, may stand in for mirrors, may sleep while backing or at speed, and still pair with mirrors and head turns.

cards.front: What does surround-view do?
cards.back: Surround-view fuses four wide cameras, nose, tail, left, and right, into a bird's-eye parking picture, yet still pairs with mirrors and head turns.

cards.front: How do rear cameras and sideview cameras differ?
cards.back: Rear cameras show astern in reverse, while sideview cameras show alongside on signal.
cards.memory_hook: Rear in reverse, sideview on signal

cards.front: How does sideview differ from surround-view?
cards.back: Sideview streams one beside lane, while surround-view stitches four cameras into a parking bird's-eye.

cards.front: What do detection alerts flag, and at what speeds?
cards.back: Detection alerts flag bikes, walkers, and obstacles at low speeds near twenty-five miles per hour, some only dead ahead and same-direction with a few auto-braking, yet never replace your own scanning, especially downtown.

cards.front: How do radar closing-gap alerts behave as you near an object?
cards.back: Radar eyes fore, aft, or both judge closing gaps with beeps, flashes, buzzes, or brake pulses that quicken as you near, turning solid-toned when impact looms.

cards.front: What do curve-speed warnings do, and what remains your job?
cards.back: Curve-speed warnings track pace and place by GPS to scold hot curve and exit entries, yet you still carry a safe speed yourself.

cards.front: What must sensors be in order to sense at all?
cards.back: Sensors must stay clean to sense at all.

cards.front: How do detection alerts and curve warnings differ?
cards.back: Detection flags bikes, walkers, and obstacles at low speed, while curve warnings flag hot entries by GPS.

cards.front: What do quickening beeps mean, and what silences every warning?
cards.back: Beeps quicken as gaps shrink, while dirty sensors silence every warning.

cards.front: What do crash warnings do for slower or stopped obstacles ahead?
cards.back: Crash warnings flag slower or stopped obstacles ahead for timely braking or swerving without braking for you, while you keep distance and caution regardless.

cards.front: How often and how far does the crash-warning system sweep, and how much warning does it give?
cards.back: The system sweeps twenty times per second out to five hundred feet, granting about three seconds of warning at fifteen to eighteen miles per hour, four seconds at eighteen to fifty miles per hour, and five seconds past fifty miles per hour

cards.front: What do crash warnings never do, and how far do they sweep?
cards.back: Crash warnings never brake for you, while their sweeps reach five hundred feet twenty times a second.

cards.front: What does the speeding alert call for?
cards.back: With current GPS data the speeding alert beeps or flashes, calling for a gentle lift or light braking rather than a slam, yet you still watch your own speed and obey limits.

cards.front: What do lane-departure warnings do, and what do they never do?
cards.back: Lane-departure warnings buzz, flash, or beep drifting cars back toward center using painted lines, yet never hold your lane for you.

cards.front: How do speed alerts and lane warnings differ?
cards.back: Speed alerts call for a gentle lift, while lane warnings lean on painted lines.
cards.memory_hook: Lift for speed, lines for lane

cards.front: What do parking sensors and cross-traffic alerts each do?
cards.back: Parking sensors beep faster as objects near with a solid tone at closest range yet miss flat, low, near, or far items, while cross-traffic alerts warn of crossing cars when backing; both still pair with mirrors, head turns, and cameras.

cards.front: What do parking sensors and cross-traffic alerts each watch for?
cards.back: Parking sensors beep at still objects, while cross-traffic alerts warn of crossing cars.

cards.front: What do assist systems do that warning systems do not?
cards.back: Assist systems shoulder part of driving, braking or steering with or for you, though you may still need to act.

cards.front: How do warning systems differ from assist systems?
cards.back: Warning systems only announce, while assist systems brake or steer with you.

cards.front: What does auto emergency braking do, and what remains yours?
cards.back: Auto emergency braking senses dawdling or halted traffic and objects ahead, braking hard when you fail to, while you keep scanning and spacing.

cards.front: What does auto reverse braking do?
cards.back: Auto reverse braking beeps or flashes at rear obstacles while backing, then brakes itself if you ignore it, yet still pairs with mirrors, head turns, and cameras.

cards.front: What does lane keeping do, and when does it quit?
cards.back: Lane keeping alerts drifting cars, then nudges the wheel home unless you override, but quits on faint, snowy, or dirty lines and never excuses your own control.

cards.front: What does left-turn avoidance do on slow lefts?
cards.back: Left-turn avoidance watches oncoming traffic on slow lefts, sounding and braking and even freezing forward motion when gaps run short, yet you still judge the turn yourself.

cards.front: How do reverse braking and lane keeping differ in what they do?
cards.back: Reverse braking halts the car for rear obstacles, while lane keeping nudges it home between lines.
cards.memory_hook: Halt for rear, nudge for lane

cards.front: When does lane keeping quit, and when does left-turn avoidance freeze motion?
cards.back: Lane keeping quits on faint paint, while left-turn avoidance freezes short gaps at slow lefts.
cards.memory_hook: Faint paint quits, short gap freezes

cards.front: What does adaptive cruise do, and what does it demand?
cards.back: Adaptive cruise holds your chosen short, medium, or long gap, slowing and even stopping and restarting in jams, yet demands your attention and rests in bad weather.

cards.front: What does auto parallel parking do, and what do you still do?
cards.back: Auto parallel parking finds the slot and talks you through pulling ahead, reversing, and releasing the wheel, while you brake, watch, and finish the alignment.

cards.front: How do adaptive cruise and auto parking differ?
cards.back: Adaptive cruise holds a following gap you set, while auto parking finds a slot you brake into.
cards.memory_hook: Cruise holds gap, parking finds slot

recap_hooks.text: Cruise holds gap, parking finds slot
